limits: Tests use explicit filesystem, bus and socket doubles; descriptor passing is not native Linux acceptance.
ACK confirms receipt of a reference only; it does not authenticate source, prove unit exit or establish cleanup.
Caller must independently authenticate the prelude, peer, source and process.
Only the install creator is connected; other five creators and complete incremental registry remain unfinished.
Per-operation maximum is 20 seconds including 2 seconds of cleanup; this does not prove the complete global runtime budget.
No production or whole-platform delivery claim.
verifiedLocally: Original install supervisor produces an opaque Origin in the same source-pinned module as its transfer Kit.
One opaque claim freezes ordinary reads and duplicate transfer claims before exchange.
Original descriptor can be transferred after unlink without fabricating a fully sealed six-role ledger.
A common frame/ACK exchange is reused by the derived existing sender.
Lost, wrong or late ACK never authorizes resend or reactivation.
Cancellation before send, during send and during ACK cannot report success.
Late received descriptors are registered before validation and attempted cleanup; close uncertainty remains sticky.
Borrowed channel ownership stays with its caller.
Producer changes are AST-checked to leave Trace and Native guards unchanged.
